nodes.label: explicar-al-implementar/SKILL.md
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.rationale: FilmAI es un proyecto académico (UTN-FRSF): el equipo aprende Django, DRF, Celery, Redis, Docker y Next.js mientras los usa. Código correcto sin explicación deja un repo que nadie puede mantener, extender ni defender en una entrega; el objetivo es que quien pidió el cambio pueda explicar qué se hizo y por qué.

nodes.label: Regla 4: Breve, pero sin perder claridad (apuntar a la versión corta y expandir donde el concepto lo pida)
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: regla 4: breve, pero sin perder claridad (apuntar a la version corta y expandir donde el concepto lo pida)
nodes.rationale: Escribir de más cansa y hace saltear la respuesta; escribir de menos deja un cambio indefendible. Explicar lo que el código no dice, no lo que ya dice. Ante la duda, explicar: la brevedad nunca se paga con una explicación que falta.

nodes.label: Regla 2: Diagrama de cajas y flechas al tocar arquitectura o comunicación entre servicios
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: regla 2: diagrama de cajas y flechas al tocar arquitectura o comunicacion entre servicios
nodes.rationale: Va antes del código cuando hay más de un servicio; cada flecha dice por dónde va (HTTP, SQL, cola de Redis) porque eso no se ve leyendo un archivo. Repetir: qué proceso corre qué código, quién habla con quién y por dónde, qué estado comparten.

nodes.label: Regla 3: Explicar cada test al escribirlo
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: regla 3: explicar cada test al escribirlo
nodes.rationale: Nunca decenas de líneas en tests.py sin saber qué se probó: por test, qué caso cubre y por qué importa. Regla inversa: un test que pasa antes y después del cambio no es un RED y hay que decirlo.

nodes.label: Regla 1: No dar por sabido ningún concepto de framework
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: regla 1: no dar por sabido ningun concepto de framework
nodes.rationale: Cada concepto (migración, volumen Docker, señal, serializer, Server Component, TTL, decorador de tarea) se explica en una línea la primera vez; si ya se explicó, se menciona y se repite compacto, sin asumir que el usuario lo recuerda.

nodes.label: Regla 7: Ofrecer opciones solo cuando son reales
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: regla 7: ofrecer opciones solo cuando son reales
nodes.rationale: Alternativas genuinas con su trade-off; cuando hay una sola respuesta razonable decirlo en vez de fabricar un menú.

nodes.label: Qué NO hace la skill: no es tutorial, no narra línea por línea, no reemplaza docs/decisiones.md
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: que no hace la skill: no es tutorial, no narra linea por linea, no reemplaza docs/decisiones.md
nodes.rationale: Las decisiones de arquitectura se registran igual en docs/decisiones.md por regla de AGENTS.md; la skill explica, no documenta.

nodes.label: Regla 5: Avanzar en unidades chicas (paso, explicación, verificación)
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: regla 5: avanzar en unidades chicas (paso, explicacion, verificacion)
nodes.rationale: No volcar todo el plan de una vez; al terminar cada paso decir qué comando correr y qué se espera ver.

nodes.label: Regla 8: Verificar antes de afirmar (TMDB, fixtures, sugerencias de bots)
nodes.author: gonzag8, marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: regla 8: verificar antes de afirmar (tmdb, fixtures, sugerencias de bots)
nodes.rationale: El repo integra la API externa TMDB: nunca afirmar qué devuelve sin consultarlo ni inventar un fixture. En C-04a un `job: "Director"` fabricado mantuvo 172 tests en verde mientras ninguna serie tenía director en producción. Las sugerencias de bots de revisión se verifican contra el archivo real.

nodes.label: Eleven allowed commit types (feat, fix, chore, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, revert)
nodes.author: marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: eleven allowed commit types (feat, fix, chore, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, revert)

nodes.label: Commit subject format `type(scope): description`
nodes.author: marcosdebona
nodes.rationale: Single canonical shape so every commit is classifiable: type restricted to 11 known values (never invent one), scope optional and names the affected area, description lowercase imperative with no trailing period; `revert:` takes no scope.

nodes.label: Pick exactly one type; most specific wins, state the alternative
nodes.author: marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: pick exactly one type; most specific wins, state the alternative
nodes.rationale: Classify against the Decision Gates table and choose one type; when two could apply choose the most specific and name the alternative so reviewers see the reasoning.

nodes.label: No AI attribution in commits (no Co-Authored-By)
nodes.author: marcosdebona
nodes.norm_label: no ai attribution in commits (no co-authored-by)
nodes.rationale: Hard rule of the project: commit messages must never carry AI attribution trailers such as Co-Authored-By.

nodes.label: Severidad MUST / SHOULD / NEVER
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.rationale: MUST violations are blocking errors with impact explained; SHOULD are non-blocking warnings; NEVER marks forbidden patterns. Every finding must cite a specific rule; non-applicable rules are skipped, never fabricated.

nodes.label: Prevent CLS (skeletons mirror content, explicit image dimensions)
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.community_name: Prevent CLS (skeletons mirror content, explicit image dimensions)
nodes.norm_label: prevent cls (skeletons mirror content, explicit image dimensions)
nodes.rationale: Skeletons must mirror final content and images need explicit dimensions so layout does not shift; preload above-fold images, lazy-load the rest.

nodes.label: Animate compositor-friendly props only (transform, opacity)
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.rationale: Never animate layout props (top/left/width/height) and never `transition: all`; prefer CSS > Web Animations API > JS libraries.

nodes.label: Visible focus rings (:focus-visible / :focus-within)
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.rationale: Never `outline: none` without a visible replacement; manage focus (trap, move, return) per APG patterns.

nodes.label: Hit target >= 24px (mobile >= 44px)
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.rationale: If the visual is smaller than 24px, expand the hit area; checkboxes/radios share one hit target with their label.

nodes.label: Honor prefers-reduced-motion
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.rationale: Provide a reduced variant or disable; animations must be interruptible and input-driven, never autoplay.

nodes.label: URL reflects state (deep-linkable filters/tabs/pagination)
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.rationale: Back/Forward must restore scroll; navigation uses <a>/<Link>, never <div onClick>.

nodes.label: Prefer APCA over WCAG 2 for contrast
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.norm_label: prefer apca over wcag 2 for contrast
nodes.rationale: MUST meet contrast and increase it on :hover/:active/:focus; APCA preferred as the perceptual model.

nodes.label: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG) patterns
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.rationale: Full keyboard support and focus management follow APG; prefer native semantics before ARIA.

nodes.label: vercel-quality SKILL
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.community_name: AGENTS.md — Reglas para agentes en FilmAI
nodes.rationale: Post-build quality gate: audits finished UI against production rules for interactions, animation, layout, accessibility, content, performance, dark mode, hydration and design. Never rewrites code; reports with severity.

nodes.label: Post-build gate: never during discovery, never rewrite code
nodes.author: vercel
nodes.norm_label: post-build gate: never during discovery, never rewrite code
nodes.rationale: Quality check runs on finished UI only and points to the rule so the implementation skill owns the fix; keeps audit and build responsibilities separate.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md (project design system source)
nodes.community_name: Visualize: direction comps & asset production (impeccable reference)
nodes.rationale: The captured visual system polish, typeset and visualize read before editing; if none exists, coherent project conventions stand in for it.

nodes.label: impeccable context (setup / capability report)
nodes.community_name: Visualize: direction comps & asset production (impeccable reference)
nodes.rationale: Runs at setup; reports NO_PRODUCT_MD when the project has no captured context and the IMAGE_TOOLS line with converters and image-generation fallback.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md (captured product context)
nodes.community_name: Visualize: direction comps & asset production (impeccable reference)
nodes.rationale: Precondition for visualize alongside DESIGN.md; `impeccable context` reports NO_PRODUCT_MD when missing and routing then leads with init.

nodes.label: Visualize: direction comps & asset production (impeccable reference)
nodes.community_name: Visualize: direction comps & asset production (impeccable reference)
nodes.norm_label: visualize: direction comps & asset production (impeccable reference)
nodes.rationale: Loaded from new-work on a comp-led build when image generation is available; a code-led contract skips it by design. Probes composition, never reopens the visual world.

nodes.label: Cache-aside lookup
nodes.rationale: SHALL return the cached JSON payload from Redis when a matching entry exists, without invoking the TMDB client.

nodes.label: Cache miss stores and returns
nodes.rationale: SHALL call TMDB when no cached entry exists, store the resulting JSON in Redis with the endpoint's TTL, and return it.

nodes.label: Graceful degradation on Redis failure
nodes.rationale: SHALL bypass the cache and call TMDB directly when Redis is unavailable (connection error or timeout); a Redis failure MUST NOT cause the request to fail.

nodes.label: JSON serialization round-trip
nodes.rationale: SHALL serialize stored entries to JSON and deserialize on retrieval so the TMDB response structure is preserved unchanged.

nodes.label: Per-endpoint TTL
nodes.rationale: SHALL apply a TTL per endpoint group: lists (trending, now_playing, discover) 6 hours; search 1 hour; details (movie_detail, tv_detail, keywords) 24 hours.

nodes.label: Stable cache key
nodes.rationale: SHALL derive the key as tmdb:{endpoint}:{params_hash}, where params_hash is a stable hash of the canonical parameters (including path arguments) so identical logical calls, even with parameters in different order, map to the same key.

nodes.label: tmdb-cache capability
nodes.rationale: Redis cache-aside layer wrapping the existing TMDBClient (C-02). Reduces TMDB API cost and latency while adding resilience: check Redis first, on miss call TMDB and store with a TTL, and when Redis is unavailable degrade gracefully by calling TMDB directly.

nodes.label: Pagination passthrough
nodes.rationale: MUST forward the page query parameter to the cache method and return TMDB's own pagination shape (page, total_pages, results) without applying DRF pagination.

nodes.label: impeccable critique-storage (latest / close)
nodes.rationale: Exit 0 returns latest snapshot body plus an exact `snapshot_file`; for local files the helper compares a content fingerprint so any byte change closes the backlog (exit 2). Close only the snapshot this pass actually processed so a newer critique's backlog stays live.

nodes.label: impeccable signals (JSON project signals)
nodes.rationale: Emits setup.hasDesign/hasCode/platform, critique.latest (score, p0, p1), git.changedFiles, devServer.running, scan.targets and scan.via so the menu can reason rather than obey a score.

nodes.label: Polish triage order (functional before cosmetic)
nodes.rationale: Broken tasks, data loss, misleading state and inaccessible paths come first; then missing states; then flow/hierarchy/responsive drift; then visual/motion; then code cleanup. Prevents perfecting one corner while the rest stays below the bar.

nodes.label: Tinted grays instead of pure gray
nodes.community_name: Tinted grays instead of pure gray
nodes.norm_label: tinted grays instead of pure gray
nodes.rationale: Warm or cool tinted grays add depth without loudness.

nodes.label: Light-on-dark compensation on three perceptual axes
nodes.community_name: Tinted grays instead of pure gray
nodes.norm_label: light-on-dark compensation on three perceptual axes
nodes.rationale: Light text on dark surfaces needs slightly more line height, a touch more tracking, and one step more weight when the face needs it.

nodes.label: impeccable build-phase (start / advance)
nodes.rationale: Phase state for the build: comps -> spec -> plates. generate-image refuses to write under .impeccable/mocks/ until start has run; advance reads the approved sidecar to close the comps phase.

nodes.label: impeccable generate-image (comps, plates, .json sidecar)
nodes.rationale: Writes comps under .impeccable/mocks/ with a .json prompt sidecar; `approved: true` in the sidecar records the approval so it survives sessions and machines that never see the brief.

nodes.label: Choose animated properties by what the transition communicates (continuity, focus/depth, reveal, material, state)
nodes.norm_label: choose animated properties by what the transition communicates (continuity, focus/depth, reveal, material, state)
nodes.rationale: Transform and opacity are reliable foundations, not the whole palette; one strong material idea carried through the focal sequence beats stacked techniques. Sibling stagger only when a list appears as a list, with capped total delay.

nodes.label: Audit Health Score: 5 dimensions × 0–4 = /20 (A11y, Performance, Theming, Responsive, Implementation Integrity) with rating bands
nodes.norm_label: audit health score: 5 dimensions × 0–4 = /20 (a11y, performance, theming, responsive, implementation integrity) with rating bands

nodes.label: Avoid animating width/height/top/left/margins; use FLIP, transforms or grid; bound blur/filter/shadow; will-change only during known animation
nodes.norm_label: avoid animating width/height/top/left/margins; use flip, transforms or grid; bound blur/filter/shadow; will-change only during known animation
nodes.rationale: Keep content visible in the default state so failed scripts don't hide the page; measure on target devices rather than assuming transform means fast; don't add a dependency for an effect the stack expresses cleanly.

nodes.label: Motion thesis: focal moment, continuity, feedback, budget
nodes.norm_label: motion thesis: focal moment, continuity, feedback, budget
nodes.rationale: Decoration without purpose is animation debt. The focal moment must come from this product and surface; a generic fade-and-rise, hover lift, parallax layer or scroll reveal is not a thesis. Do not animate a static area merely because it exists.

nodes.label: Every web animation needs a prefers-reduced-motion path with an intentional alternative
nodes.norm_label: every web animation needs a prefers-reduced-motion path with an intentional alternative
nodes.rationale: Reduce or remove spatial movement while preserving opacity, color and state transitions that carry meaning; reduced motion means fewer and gentler animations, not disabling all motion. Nonessential loops stop when offscreen.

nodes.label: Timing bands 100–150 / 150–300 / 300–500 / 500–800 ms; exit faster than entrance; cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
nodes.norm_label: timing bands 100–150 / 150–300 / 300–500 / 500–800 ms; exit faster than entrance; cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
nodes.rationale: Timing expresses distance and consequence; bounce/elastic curves not by reflex; long feedback feels like latency.

nodes.label: A11y check: prefers-reduced-motion needs an intentional alternative; flag a global 0.01ms kill
nodes.norm_label: a11y check: prefers-reduced-motion needs an intentional alternative; flag a global 0.01ms kill
nodes.rationale: A blanket kill destroys useful feedback; also flag flashing above threshold and motion that blocks focus, reading or task completion.

nodes.label: Performance check: will-change is a targeted hint for known expensive animations, not a baseline
nodes.norm_label: performance check: will-change is a targeted hint for known expensive animations, not a baseline

nodes.label: Motion: one authored moment, not scattered effects nor one identical entrance on every section
nodes.norm_label: motion: one authored moment, not scattered effects nor one identical entrance on every section
nodes.rationale: Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default; reach past transform and opacity (blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, shadow) when they stay smooth.

nodes.label: Detector result is defect evidence, not proof of quality
nodes.community_name: Detector result is defect evidence, not proof of quality
nodes.norm_label: detector result is defect evidence, not proof of quality
nodes.rationale: A clean mechanical scan is a floor, not a verdict; the rendered experience and real interaction path must be inspected.

nodes.label: Drift classification (missing token / one-off / conceptual mismatch / local defect)
nodes.community_name: Drift classification (missing token / one-off / conceptual mismatch / local defect)
nodes.norm_label: drift classification (missing token / one-off / conceptual mismatch / local defect)
nodes.rationale: Classifying each drift before fixing lets the fix land at the narrowest correct level: promote a token, swap in a shared component, realign the flow, or just complete the local implementation.

nodes.label: ease-out-quart easing (never bounce or elastic)
nodes.rationale: Understated motion: shorter distances (10-20px), gentle easing, functional motion only.

nodes.label: Never gray text on a colored background
nodes.community_name: Never gray text on a colored background
nodes.norm_label: never gray text on a colored background
nodes.rationale: Use a darker shade of the background color or transparency instead of gray on color.

nodes.label: impeccable detect (bundled HTML/CSS rule engine)
nodes.rationale: Local detector over markup/style files: no network, no npx, web-only. Hits steer picks (quality/contrast -> audit/polish; gradient text/eyebrows -> quieter/typeset; flat palette -> colorize). Skipped for ios/android/adaptive.

nodes.label: Never auto-run a recommended command
nodes.rationale: The recommendation is the lede but the user confirms; keeps agency with the person even when signals are strong.

nodes.label: live and detect are web-only
nodes.rationale: The browser overlay and the HTML rule engine do not apply to native app code, so ios/android/adaptive projects are never led toward them.

nodes.label: Never ask for CSS values or canned aesthetic lanes
nodes.community_name: Never ask for CSS values or canned aesthetic lanes
nodes.norm_label: never ask for css values or canned aesthetic lanes
nodes.rationale: Visual-world and concept choices belong to new-work, so discovery stays on purpose, people, outcome, material and boundaries.

nodes.label: 1rem / 16px body floor
nodes.rationale: Ordinary web body floor unless a dense role, platform convention or user setting justifies otherwise; preserves zoom and user font settings.

nodes.label: --p-scale live signature parameter
nodes.rationale: Every live variant declares a coarse `scale` range (0.85-1.3) and authors its type ramp against var(--p-scale, 1); at most one extra pairing/weight parameter.

nodes.label: Reading measure 45-75ch
nodes.rationale: Keep prose in 45-75 characters; tune line height inversely with measure because wider lines need more leading.

nodes.label: Typographic role scale (purpose-named tokens)
nodes.rationale: Fewest roles and families that make hierarchy unmistakable; role names describe purpose rather than values; repeated roles stay identical across screens.

nodes.label: A comp is a designed surface, not a picture of the subject
nodes.community_name: A comp is a designed surface, not a picture of the subject
nodes.norm_label: a comp is a designed surface, not a picture of the subject
nodes.rationale: Prompts lead with the surface's own structure or the model paints the subject instead of its website; the inverse (a surface with none of its subject) also fails. Busy is louder, not bolder.

nodes.label: impeccable comp-spec (region boxes, crops, plate prompts)
nodes.community_name: impeccable comp-spec (region boxes, crops, plate prompts)
nodes.norm_label: impeccable comp-spec (region boxes, crops, plate prompts)
nodes.rationale: Turns the approved comp into region boxes with sampled palettes; a region's medium follows from what the pixels are (figures, textures, shaded illustration -> raster plate; text, controls, chrome, flat shapes -> semantic). Dropping an image-native region is a user scope decision, never a silent flattening.

nodes.label: North-star comp (three compositional options)
nodes.rationale: Three is the number: one comp invites rubber-stamping, the spread between three surfaces the composition worth building. Comps are the build thread's own work and are comped at the surface's own viewport.

nodes.label: Raster provenance (embed-prompt + spec row)
nodes.rationale: Every raster the artifact references carries its generation prompt inside the file (`impeccable embed-prompt`) plus its row in the spec; sourced rasters embed their origin instead.

nodes.label: impeccable serve-question (decision page)
nodes.rationale: Shows the three comps together, one option per comp with the comp as hero; fallback when the structured question tool errors. Only after both fail may the choice be treated as delegated.

nodes.label: openspec spec-writing rules
nodes.rationale: Specs MUST use Given/When/Then scenarios and RFC 2119 keywords (MUST, SHALL, SHOULD, MAY). Proposals include a rollback plan for risky changes; designs include sequence diagrams and documented architecture decisions with rationale; tasks grouped by phase with hierarchical numbering; before declaring done run `ruff format . && ruff check .` (backend) and `npx prettier --check .` (frontend); verify has a 400-line review budget and ask-on-risk delivery; archive warns before merging destructive deltas.

nodes.label: strict TDD policy
nodes.rationale: strict_tdd: true. Backend tests run with the Django test runner (`python manage.py test`, unit + integration, no e2e, no coverage threshold). Frontend has no test runner at all.

nodes.label: catalog-daily-sync capability
nodes.rationale: Scheduled maintenance of the local catalog (CU-021, C-04b): a nightly Celery task grows the corpus without waiting for a user to open anything, refreshes rows TMDB reports as changed, and a second task recovers embedding work that never completed. Builds on catalog-materialization, which owns the single write path. Initial ~10k seed is C-04c; real embedding provider is B-06.

nodes.label: Discovery pass
nodes.rationale: The sync MUST walk a declared set of TMDB listing sources and materialize each supported item so the corpus grows without user activity. Each source declares how the TMDB type is resolved (media_type for mixed endpoints, otherwise implied). Items that are neither movie nor tv (trending includes person) MUST be skipped and counted as omitidas, not treated as errors.

nodes.label: Embedding backfill
nodes.rationale: MUST provide catalogo.backfill_embeddings(limite=...) because materializar() enqueues an embedding only when it creates the row, so pending (broker down) or failed (provider error) rows would never be retried. Covers two populations under one shared limit: pending/failed rows, and ready rows whose recomputed source_hash or model_version no longer matches. processing rows MUST NOT be touched. It MUST re-enqueue generar_embedding rather than compute vectors, keeping the claim logic of embedding-infrastructure the single source of idempotency; a ready row selected for regeneration is returned to pending first because the claim only accepts pending/failed.

nodes.label: Failures are per item
nodes.rationale: A failure processing one item MUST NOT abort the run: it is logged, counted in errores, and the run continues. If the change list itself fails for one TMDB type, that type's refresh is skipped and the run continues, including discovery.

nodes.label: Refresh pass driven by TMDB's change list
nodes.norm_label: refresh pass driven by tmdb's change list
nodes.rationale: MUST refresh the rows TMDB reports as modified rather than inferring staleness from elapsed time: read /movie/changes and /tv/changes, intersect with locally stored ids in Python over two sets (not a huge SQL IN clause), and re-materialize the intersection with forzar=True. Changed ids not in the local DB MUST NOT be materialized or the sync becomes a crawl of all TMDB. Pagination stops at a declared maximum; ids beyond the cap are covered by the staleness safety net.

nodes.label: Refresh precedes discovery
nodes.rationale: The refresh pass MUST run before the discovery pass. A title in theatres is both actively edited on TMDB and present in listing sources; discovery-first would enrich it as new and the refresh would enrich it again moments later.

nodes.label: Rows are processed oldest first
nodes.rationale: Both backfill populations MUST be traversed by ascending fecha_actualizacion so rows beyond the limit in one run are reached in a later one instead of being starved indefinitely.

nodes.label: Run statistics
nodes.rationale: Each run MUST return and log nuevas, ya_existentes, refrescadas, omitidas and errores. ya_existentes counts presence (rows discovery met that were already stored) and MUST NOT be read as 'updated'; refrescadas counts re-enrichment and is the only counter guaranteeing a write, named for the action because TMDB may report a change in a field this project does not store. refrescadas is the 'cantidad de producciones actualizadas' of CU-021 step 5. nuevas counts each production once across sources; a production MAY appear in two counters because each pass counts independently.

nodes.label: The sync writes only through materialization
nodes.norm_label: the sync writes only through materialization
nodes.rationale: sync_catalogo_diaria MUST NOT write ProduccionAudiovisual rows itself; every item goes through materializar(). A TMDB listing item MUST NOT be treated as sufficient to fill a row: listing payloads carry genre_ids instead of genre names and no status, runtime, credits or keywords, i.e. four of the six sections of the canonical embedding text.

nodes.label: User data survives synchronization
nodes.rationale: The sync MUST update only TMDB-sourced fields; ratings, reviews and list membership are untouched. Refresh MUST update the existing row in place; delete-and-reinsert MUST NOT be used because Calificacion and list entries cascade from ProduccionAudiovisual and recreating a row would silently destroy user data.

nodes.label: catalog-materialization capability
nodes.rationale: On-demand, concurrency-safe persistence of ProduccionAudiovisual (CU-021, C-04a): any production opened through a catalog detail endpoint is stored globally and enriched from TMDB so it can later be rated, added to lists (Módulo 3) and retrieved semantically (B-06). Scheduled bulk sync and backfill are C-04b; real provider is B-06.

nodes.label: Concurrency safety
nodes.rationale: Two simultaneous materializations MUST both succeed and converge on the same row: the losing insert recovers by reading the winner. The insert MUST be wrapped in transaction.atomic() so the constraint violation rolls back to a savepoint (PostgreSQL aborts the whole transaction otherwise and the recovery query would fail too). An IntegrityError not from this race (row still absent) MUST propagate rather than be disguised as 'already existed'.

nodes.label: Enrichment is recorded, not inferred
nodes.rationale: Each row records when it last pulled the full TMDB detail in ProduccionAudiovisual.fecha_enriquecimiento; NULL means never enriched and forces enrichment on next materialization regardless of other fields. Completeness MUST NOT be inferred from content fields. Revised 16/09/2026 (C-04b): the old criterion 'row has no titulo' only held while a single writer filled every column; a listing-shaped row has a title but no genres, cast, crew or keywords and would have counted as complete forever. The timestamp MUST be written in the same save() as the enriched fields so a failed write never leaves a row marked enriched.

nodes.label: Forced refresh
nodes.rationale: materializar() MUST accept forzar=True, re-enriching even when completeness and staleness checks would skip. This is the only sanctioned way to refresh a complete row: callers MUST NOT blank fecha_enriquecimiento to provoke the path nor write the row themselves.

nodes.label: Single materialization entry point
nodes.rationale: Exactly one write path into ProduccionAudiovisual: catalogo.services.materialization.materializar(id_tmdb, tipo_tmdb, forzar=False). Callers MUST NOT insert rows directly nor call TMDB themselves, including bulk processes like the daily sync, which iterate and call the helper per item. Accepts TMDB vocabulary (movie/tv) and translates to TipoProduccion via catalogo.services.adapter; unsupported types raise ValueError before any write.

nodes.label: Staleness safety net
nodes.rationale: Re-enrich a row whose fecha_enriquecimiento is older than a long window (_DIAS_RED_DE_SEGURIDAD, 90 days). NOT the primary refresh mechanism: actual change detection belongs to the daily sync, which asks TMDB's changes list and forces a refresh through forzar. The window only guarantees a row can never go unrefreshed forever if that list is missed.

nodes.label: Task idempotency
nodes.rationale: Celery guarantees at-least-once delivery, so generar_embedding MUST tolerate double delivery or two workers at once: no-op when the row is already ready with the same source_hash and model_version; claim the row with a conditional atomic UPDATE from pending/failed to processing and no-op when zero rows are affected; leave ready rows alone so a usable vector is never downgraded because a provider is momentarily down.

nodes.label: Known limitations of the daily sync
nodes.norm_label: known limitations of the daily sync
nodes.rationale: A row stranded in processing (worker killed mid-task) is recovered by nobody; a lease with expiry is the fix, deferred until B-06 makes tasks long enough for it to matter. If the provider fails while regenerating a stale ready row it ends in failed with its previous vector, unused by search for one night and retried next run. Discovery reads only page 1 of each source, capturing novelty rather than volume; bulk population is C-04c.

nodes.label: Check 6: Floor (craft-floor Refuse list)
nodes.rationale: Exists because hookless harnesses reach the reviewer with no detector findings; a banned element is a material fix even when it matches the comp.

nodes.label: impeccable context (session boot)
nodes.rationale: Boot command that resolves PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md paths, reports UPDATE_AVAILABLE, IMAGE_GEN_AVAILABLE and MANUAL_DETECTOR_REQUIRED, and runs the cheap staleness subset once a week per project (stalenessCheck: false or IMPECCABLE_NO_STALENESS_CHECK=1 silence it).

nodes.label: Tool version drift
nodes.rationale: Installed skill older than published; reported at boot as UPDATE_AVAILABLE and fixed by npx impeccable update, not doctor's job.

nodes.label: Design detector hook (post-tool-use)
nodes.rationale: Runs the impeccable design detector on edits to design-relevant files and pushes a system reminder; Cursor blocks via preToolUse, Claude Code/Codex/Copilot remind post-edit, Grok surfaces on Stop.

nodes.label: Ignore scoping (ignore-value < file-scoped value < ignore-file < ignore-rule)
nodes.norm_label: ignore scoping (ignore-value < file-scoped value < ignore-file < ignore-rule)
nodes.rationale: Self-serve stops at ignore-value; ignore-file and ignore-rule silence too much to add on the agent's own judgment and need the user; inline impeccable-disable comments only when the waiver must travel with a file leaving the repo.

nodes.label: .impeccable/config.json (unified project config)
nodes.rationale: Shared committed config: hook runtime settings under hook, detector ignores and extensions under detector, buildPath, stalenessCheck, projectRoots.

nodes.label: impeccable detect (manual CLI design scan)
nodes.rationale: Uses the same project filter config as the hook by default; --no-config gives a raw run; hook.enabled controls only automatic execution.

nodes.label: Triage findings (fix / narrow ignore / ask once)
nodes.norm_label: triage findings (fix / narrow ignore / ask once)
nodes.rationale: Real problems get fixed, never ignored to push a write through; confident false positives get the narrowest ignore with named evidence in --reason; unsure findings stand and earn one question.

nodes.label: Two-tier detector rules (immediate vs Stop deep pass)
nodes.norm_label: two-tier detector rules (immediate vs stop deep pass)
nodes.rationale: Per-edit hook surfaces only mechanical, unambiguous problems worth interrupting for; taste rules (copy cadence, palette, rhythm) are deferred to a Stop deep pass over all touched UI files, deduplicated; hook.perEditRules: all restores the full set per edit.

nodes.label: Two isolated assessments (layout judgment vs mechanical scan)
nodes.norm_label: two isolated assessments (layout judgment vs mechanical scan)
nodes.rationale: Run the human layout assessment and the detector scan independently and synthesize afterwards; keep mechanical evidence out of the first pass because a clean scan cannot prove hierarchy or rhythm.

nodes.label: $impeccable hooks
nodes.rationale: Manages the design detector hook per project by editing .impeccable/config.json through the admin script; never hand-edits the config except the detector.extensions field.

nodes.label: Not-canonized defects line

This MUST NOT alter the response contract: the body stays raw TMDB passthrough; a materialization failure is logged and swallowed, never surfaced, so the catalog remains readable even when local persistence is degraded. nodes.rationale: Lets the user move from neutral to the variant's full color strategy without regeneration; at most two extra variant-specific params.

nodes.label: Visitor mode for color: Persuade/Experience may own large regions; Operate/Read encode action, selection, status, wayfinding (rarity gives an accent force)
nodes.norm_label: visitor mode for color: persuade/experience may own large regions; operate/read encode action, selection, status, wayfinding (rarity gives an accent force)

nodes.label: Neutral dominance / 10% color accent rule
nodes.rationale: Let neutrals do most of the work and use color only as accent so contrast lands where it matters most.

nodes.label: Visitor modes: Persuade / Operate / Read / Experience
nodes.norm_label: visitor modes: persuade / operate / read / experience
nodes.rationale: The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface and is chosen from the requested surface, not the product (a tool's landing page is Persuade; a fashion house's docs are Read). Persisted only in the surface brief.

nodes.label: Material color roles + Dynamic Color (Material You) with static fallback; tonal elevation
nodes.norm_label: material color roles + dynamic color (material you) with static fallback; tonal elevation
nodes.rationale: Role tokens (primary, on-primary, surface, surface-variant, outline, error) resolve light/dark and contrast variants automatically; raw hex breaks there. Dark theme is a first-class scheme, never a quick invert; elevation via standard surface tonal levels, no arbitrary drop shadows.

nodes.label: Build color roles (canvas/elevated surfaces, text, action/focus/selection, borders, semantic, data), not a bag of swatches
nodes.norm_label: build color roles (canvas/elevated surfaces, text, action/focus/selection, borders, semantic, data), not a bag of swatches
nodes.rationale: Let the strongest color own a deliberate region or role instead of scattering tiny accents; keep the primary action's color for the action; define primitives and semantic tokens so theme changes remap roles.

nodes.label: Dark mode: design surface elevation and contrast explicitly; do not invert the light theme mechanically
nodes.norm_label: dark mode: design surface elevation and contrast explicitly; do not invert the light theme mechanically

nodes.label: Prefer OKLCH for a new web palette
nodes.norm_label: prefer oklch for a new web palette
nodes.rationale: Lightness and chroma can be adjusted predictably; when deriving ramps vary lightness and reduce chroma near white and black rather than keeping high chroma at extreme lightness for uniform math. Hue comes from product meaning, never a default category association.

nodes.label: Disposition vocabulary (recapture/rebuild/fix/ship)
nodes.rationale: Four words, derived never felt: recapture when the evidence check failed, rebuild when the rebuild-directive fired, fix when material_fixes is non-empty, ship only when the matrix holds no contradicted or missing row. The parent reports it verbatim with no authority to soften.

nodes.label: Check 0: Evidence (capture validity)
nodes.rationale: A required capture that is absent fails exactly like a malformed one; a verdict derived from a broken capture launders the breakage into an approval, so any failure forces disposition: recapture and stops the review.

nodes.label: Fidelity element matrix (TYPE / MATERIAL / GROUND rows)
nodes.norm_label: fidelity element matrix (type / material / ground rows)
nodes.rationale: Every salient comp element classified match / adaptation / missing / contradicted / added; TYPE, MATERIAL and GROUND rows are mandatory because imitation material is the most reliable mark of machine-made design and ground drift toward the rendition prior (warm cream, blue-black slate) is the direction to hunt.

nodes.label: Rebuild directive
nodes.rationale: When MATERIAL is contradicted on the focal element or contradiction is the page rather than the exception, stop ordering repairs: a list of patches against a rejected page launders the rejection into an approval.

nodes.label: Verdict Pass (scoring fixes resolved/partial/unresolved)
nodes.rationale: Post-fix recaptures are scored, not re-hunted; the parent's narration is not evidence; a ship earned here covers the scored fixes only, never the whole surface.

nodes.label: buildPath workflow setting (comp-first vs code-first)
nodes.rationale: Asked once when image generation exists and nothing is recorded; comp-first sets the bar with an image the build must match, code-first writes ambition into the direction contract. It is a workflow setting written only from the user's answer, never from silence, and never into PRODUCT.md.

nodes.label: impeccable build-phase state machine (comps, spec, plates, hero, sections, motion, responsive)
nodes.norm_label: impeccable build-phase state machine (comps, spec, plates, hero, sections, motion, responsive)
nodes.rationale: Each phase closes via build-phase advance; exit 2 means the gate failed and printed why; nothing is written for a later phase while an earlier gate is open.

nodes.label: Challenger verdicts (wins / competitive / declined) and raises
nodes.norm_label: challenger verdicts (wins / competitive / declined) and raises
nodes.rationale: Fuse each challenger before judging on exactly two axes (audience identification, product clarity); a declined challenger still donates one discipline as a named raise line, never its clothes.

nodes.label: Code-led build
nodes.rationale: No comp and no apology: ambition lives in the FIRST VIEWPORT block and named signature interaction, audited in behavior by the finish reviewer; the chosen decision comp rides along as critique reference only.

nodes.label: Comp-led build (comp as measured contract)
nodes.rationale: Models systematically believe their HTML/CSS/SVG recreation of an image succeeded when it did not, so the build runs as a state machine whose gates measure the screen against the comp; frontier-tier work, smaller models stall at the hero gate.

nodes.label: Comp spec (impeccable comp-spec regions, palette, medium)
nodes.norm_label: comp spec (impeccable comp-spec regions, palette, medium)
nodes.rationale: Every comp region is named by grid span with a kind (plate/image/texture vs text/control/chrome) and a note; unnamed ink can never be missing, so everything the comp shows gets a region, and anything not in the spec does not exist on the page.

nodes.label: concept-seed roll (impeccable concept-seed)
nodes.rationale: The dice assign the direction to build and deal catalog challengers so every run does not converge on the category default; skipping it on a new or replacement world is a contract violation, and a user- or brief-pinned direction always beats the roll.

nodes.label: Decision page (impeccable serve-question)
nodes.rationale: Cards of equal anatomy (thesis, palette, materials, first viewport, honest risk) with steer, re-roll and the buildPath toggle; exit 2 routes to the structured question tool, exit 4 means closed unanswered.

nodes.label: Direction contract (THESIS / OWN-WORLD / STORY / FIRST VIEWPORT / FORM / FINISH)
nodes.norm_label: direction contract (thesis / own-world / story / first viewport / form / finish)
nodes.rationale: Development-only contract recorded in the surface brief before code; never copied into any browser-delivered artifact because a compiler stripping metadata is not a safety boundary; the finish reviewer audits the render against it.

nodes.label: impeccable font-match (measure and rank display faces)
nodes.norm_label: impeccable font-match (measure and rank display faces)
nodes.rationale: Type is measured, not guessed: cap height, width class and weight are read off comp pixels and ranked against a Google Fonts fingerprint index; the gate accepts only what font-match wrote.

nodes.label: Hero gate (72% comp-diff, no hard veto)
nodes.norm_label: hero gate (72% comp-diff, no hard veto)
nodes.rationale: First viewport at the comp's dimensions with plates placed before text; passes at 72% overall with no missing region, contradicted plate, SVG illustration or invented ink; a third attempt that only nudges values on the same region is refused. This is where the run's ambition is won or lost.

nodes.label: IMPECCABLE'S PICK card
nodes.rationale: One card for the agent's top-ranked grounded candidate when it is not the assigned direction, never in lead position, with an honest familiarity risk; one pick, never a ranked list that hands selection back to a taste function.

nodes.label: Memory test (first viewport as thesis)
nodes.rationale: If someone left after one viewport, what would they describe an hour later? A mood means the concept has not committed.

nodes.label: Plates (raster regions shipped as generated assets)
nodes.norm_label: plates (raster regions shipped as generated assets)
nodes.rationale: Every painted region is regenerated at asset resolution from its comp crop; a crop of the comp is a reference, never a shipping pixel; page code waits for this gate because a page written before its plates draws its material in CSS.

nodes.label: QUALITY BAR card / board
nodes.rationale: Sets the craft level (finish, commitment, art direction) the build must reach; governs commitment and finish, never composition.

nodes.label: Raster provenance (impeccable embed-prompt)
nodes.rationale: Every shipping raster carries its generation prompt or origin; embed-prompt --scan reports missing provenance and only reads, deletion is reserved for rasters a round abandoned.

nodes.label: Re-roll registers (plain / safer / bolder)
nodes.rationale: The register is the user's steering on the familiar-to-bold axis; a user saying bolder or safer while a direction round is open means these registers, not the bolder or harden commands.

nodes.label: Standing exit (the canon, played straight)
nodes.rationale: Every direction round offers the category standard as the user's door, never recommended or weighed against the roll; when taken, convention becomes the commitment at competitor craft level and is recorded as a brand commitment in PRODUCT.md.

nodes.label: Surface brief (impeccable surface-brief read/write)
nodes.rationale: Small: scope and visitor mode, audience, job, proof, constraints, chosen direction and the direction contract; never copies product truth or DESIGN.md tokens.

nodes.label: Impeccable Finish Reviewer (inline degraded role)
nodes.rationale: Fresh eyes on a done artifact outside the build thread's attention gravity; edits nothing, has no browser, reviews only from provided captures and files.

nodes.label: New visual work (new-work flow)
nodes.rationale: For a new surface or replacement identity: PRODUCT.md owns product truth, DESIGN.md owns durable visual decisions, a surface brief keeps strategy for one route; a local addition never becomes a new identity exercise.

nodes.label: FINISH line (unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished)
nodes.norm_label: finish line (unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished)
nodes.rationale: Closes the direction contract verbatim so later agents reloading the brief know a page that looks complete with FINISH undischarged is abandoned at the finish line, not done.

nodes.label: Truth binds claims, not demonstrations
nodes.rationale: Author illustrative material at full fidelity and label it synthetic; prices, customers, benchmarks and capabilities stay uninventable. Refusing a bold direction because demo data does not exist is the timidity reflex wearing honesty's clothes.

nodes.label: django-allauth[socialaccount]==65.19.1 (pin exacto)
nodes.rationale: Pin exacto porque `allauth.account.internal.flows.email_verification`, usado por usuarios.views.ConfirmarCorreoView, no es API pública y puede cambiar entre releases menores; 65.19.1 es la versión instalada y probada en el contenedor.

nodes.label: backend
nodes.rationale: Django + DRF HTTP server. Runs as the host user (${UID:-1000}:${GID:-1000}) instead of root so files generated inside the container (startapp, pycache) stay editable without sudo. Mounts ./backend for real hot-reload. Waits for db and redis to be healthy. It is the only container that runs migrations and creates the superuser.

nodes.label: celery-beat
nodes.rationale: The clock that fires scheduled tasks (C-04b). Executes nothing: at the time set in CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE (settings.py) it publishes the task to the Redis queue and celery-worker picks it up. Separate container because there must be EXACTLY ONE beat: two clocks = every task fired twice (tasks are idempotent so nothing corrupts, but TMDB traffic would double). Uses --schedule=/tmp/celerybeat-schedule so the state file does not land in the ./backend bind mount and appear in the repo; losing it on recreate is fine because beat recomputes from the schedule. No watchmedo: beat only reads the schedule from settings.py, which rarely changes; `docker compose restart celery-beat` picks up edits.

nodes.label: celery-worker
nodes.rationale: Same image as backend (same code and deps) but instead of the HTTP server it runs the process that consumes the Redis task queue (today: generar_embedding, C-04a). Wrapped in `watchmedo auto-restart` because Celery, unlike Django's runserver, never reloads code: without it the worker silently keeps executing the old in-memory version of every edited task. Development-only wrapper; production deploys a new image and runs celery directly. RUN_MIGRATIONS=false so only the backend container touches the schema.

nodes.label: db
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 16 from the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image because ProduccionEmbedding (C-04a) needs the pgvector extension precompiled. pgvector publishes only Debian (glibc) variants, not Alpine (musl), so adopting it requires recreating the pgdata volume: text-collation rules of the indexes differ between the two libc implementations. Healthcheck via pg_isready gates dependent services.

nodes.label: filmai_network
nodes.rationale: Internal bridge network: services resolve each other by service name (backend connects to PostgreSQL with host=db, not localhost).

nodes.label: frontend
nodes.rationale: Next.js 15 + Tailwind + Shadcn dev server. Same host-UID reasoning as backend. Next.js only exposes NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables to the browser, so the global GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID is re-exported as NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID. An anonymous /app/node_modules volume prevents the bind mount from overwriting the container's node_modules.

nodes.label: Named volumes pgdata and redisdata
nodes.rationale: Named volumes persist database and Redis data across `docker compose down`; only `down -v` destroys them.

nodes.label: redis
nodes.rationale: Redis 7 (alpine) serving two roles: TMDB response cache and Celery broker/result backend. Persisted in the redisdata named volume; healthcheck via redis-cli ping.

nodes.label: Scheduled execution
nodes.rationale: MUST run catalogo.sync_catalogo_diaria daily at 03:00 and catalogo.backfill_embeddings at 04:00 through a dedicated celery-beat service in docker-compose.yml. CELERY_TIMEZONE MUST be explicit so the schedule is not interpreted in UTC. Exactly one beat instance MUST run and it MUST NOT write its schedule state file into the source bind mount. Beat only enqueues; a celery-worker executes.

nodes.label: TMDB enrichment
nodes.rationale: New or incomplete rows MUST be populated from the TMDB detail, credits and keywords endpoints via TMDBClientCache, outside any open write transaction because network calls may take seconds. Field mapping follows type-specific shapes (title/name, release_date/first_air_date with empty => NULL, first 10 cast, keywords under `keywords` for movies and `results` for TV, runtime vs episode_run_time[0]). Two live-API asymmetries confirmed 2026-09-15: series carry no job=='Director' in crew (directors are per-episode) so authorship MUST come from created_by or every series would ship an empty Directors line; episode_run_time is frequently empty so duracion is legitimately NULL, accepted because duration is not embedded.

nodes.label: Broker topology
nodes.rationale: Celery's broker and result backend MUST live on Redis logical databases separate from the TMDB response cache so clearing one never destroys the other: DB 0 = TMDB cache, DB 1 = Celery broker, DB 2 = Celery results.

nodes.label: embedding-infrastructure capability
nodes.rationale: Minimal Celery + pgvector plumbing so the catalog can enqueue embedding work without blocking a request, with the actual provider left as a documented extension point. Advanced inside C-04a so materialization has somewhere to enqueue to; the real provider (Ollama / bge-m3) and semantic retrieval are B-06.

nodes.label: Provider call isolation
nodes.rationale: The provider call MUST happen outside any open transaction (may take seconds, must not hold a connection or block writers). The task MUST NOT raise: any provider failure leaves the row in failed and is logged. Propagating would make Celery retry in a loop and add nothing, since the production stays visible either way.

nodes.label: Detail Methods
nodes.rationale: MUST provide get_movie_detail(id_tmdb) -> /movie/{id}, get_tv_detail(id_tmdb) -> /tv/{id}, and get_keywords(id_tmdb, tipo) -> /{tipo}/{id}/keywords, returning parsed JSON.

nodes.label: Next.js create-next-app README
nodes.rationale: Unmodified boilerplate from create-next-app: dev server on localhost:3000, edit app/page.tsx, next/font loads Geist, deploy on Vercel. Carries no project-specific instructions; the real frontend conventions live in docs/ and CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: FilmAI project context
nodes.rationale: Context handed to openspec: UTN-FRSF movie/series review platform with AI recommendations. Django 5.1 + DRF 3.15 (Python 3.12) with apps catalogo, chatbot, listas, usuarios; Next.js 15 App Router + React 19 + Tailwind v4 + Shadcn; PostgreSQL 16 + Redis 7 + Celery via docker-compose. docs/01-06 and docs/decisiones.md are the source of truth (Spanish); custom user model usuarios.Usuario. Note: it still says '4 services' although docker-compose.yml now declares six.

nodes.label: TMDB field mapping table
nodes.rationale: Movie vs TV source per field: titulo (title/name), fecha_lanzamiento (release_date/first_air_date, empty => NULL), reparto (first 10 credits.cast), directores (crew job=='Director' / created_by with crew fallback), generos (genres[].name), keywords (`keywords` / `results`), duracion (runtime / episode_run_time[0] else NULL), cantidad_temporadas/episodios (NULL / number_of_seasons, number_of_episodes), poster (raw poster_path; CDN URL built by frontend).

nodes.label: Discovery Methods
nodes.rationale: MUST provide get_trending(media_type='all', time_window='week', page=1) -> /trending/{media_type}/{time_window}, get_now_playing(page=1) -> /movie/now_playing, and discover(tipo, genero, anio, min_rating, page) -> /discover/{tipo}, each returning parsed JSON.

nodes.label: Retry Policy
nodes.rationale: MUST retry only transitory errors (429, 5xx, transport failures) with backoff honoring Retry-After; MUST NOT retry other 4xx; retries MUST be bounded to avoid infinite loops.

nodes.label: Search
nodes.rationale: MUST provide search(query, tipo, page) returning parsed JSON from /search/{tipo}.

nodes.label: Thin Client
nodes.rationale: MUST return raw parsed JSON and MUST NOT map responses to Django models. Tests MUST use httpx.MockTransport, never real network calls.

nodes.label: tmdb-client capability
nodes.rationale: TMDBClient is a thin httpx-based wrapper over TMDB API v3 for live catalog discovery (C-01). Returns raw parsed JSON with no Django model mapping (that is C-04a). Auth via api_key query parameter. Redis cache (C-02), endpoints (C-03), materialization (C-04a), Celery sync (C-04b) and UI are out of scope.

nodes.label: Delight thesis
nodes.rationale: One sentence stating what the user should feel and why that feeling belongs to this product, then the smallest system that can deliver it, derived from product mechanism and visual world rather than a stock catalog.

nodes.label: Emotional moments (success, waiting, empty, error, repeat, discovery)
nodes.norm_label: emotional moments (success, waiting, empty, error, repeat, discovery)
nodes.rationale: Concentrate delight where it is earned: match success response to effort, never fake work while waiting, lead error states with recovery, keep repeat interactions satisfying after the hundredth use.

nodes.label: Progressive disclosure (distill)
nodes.rationale: Hide complexity behind clear entry points (accordions, modals, step-through flows) so everything is not visible at once.

nodes.label: Error handling (network, API status codes, form validation)
nodes.norm_label: error handling (network, api status codes, form validation)

nodes.label: Internationalization hardening (text expansion, RTL, CJK, Intl API)
nodes.norm_label: internationalization hardening (text expansion, rtl, cjk, intl api)
nodes.rationale: Budget 30-40% for translations, use logical CSS properties for RTL, format dates and numbers with Intl, use a plural-aware i18n library instead of English suffix logic.

nodes.label: Text overflow and wrapping
nodes.rationale: Ellipsis, line-clamp, break-word, min-width: 0 on flex/grid items, and a 16px mobile body floor because iOS Safari force-zooms focused inputs under 16px.

nodes.label: Empty state design (what, why, how, visual, help)
nodes.norm_label: empty state design (what, why, how, visual, help)
nodes.rationale: Every empty state says what will be here, why it matters, how to start, with visual interest and contextual help; types: first use, user cleared, no results, no permissions, error.

nodes.label: Time to value / aha moment
nodes.rationale: Front-load the 20% that delivers 80% of value; teach in context not upfront; make onboarding skippable and never show it twice.

nodes.label: Component state vocabulary (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error)
nodes.norm_label: component state vocabulary (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error)
nodes.rationale: Every interactive component ships all states; skeletons over spinners, empty states that teach, overlays that escape overflow-hidden containers.

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement is non-negotiable (overdrive)
nodes.rationale: Every technique degrades gracefully via @supports and capability checks (WebGPU -> WebGL2 -> CSS); the experience without the enhancement must still be good.

nodes.label: Propose before building (2-3 directions, user picks)
nodes.norm_label: propose before building (2-3 directions, user picks)
nodes.rationale: Overdrive has the highest misfire potential, so directions with their trade-offs are put inside the question itself and no code is written until the user confirms one.

nodes.label: View Transitions API and browser toolkit
nodes.norm_label: view transitions api and browser toolkit

nodes.label: $impeccable delight
nodes.rationale: Delight is product character revealed through a useful interaction, not a layer of generic whimsy; generic whimsy is worse than neutral clarity.

nodes.label: $impeccable harden
nodes.rationale: Designs that only work with perfect data are not production-ready; harden against real inputs, errors, languages and network conditions.

nodes.label: $impeccable onboard
nodes.rationale: Onboarding's job is not to teach the product but to get people to the moment that proves it is worth their time.

nodes.label: $impeccable optimize
nodes.rationale: Performance is a feature; identify the actual bottleneck for this interface, fix it, then measure.

nodes.label: $impeccable overdrive
nodes.rationale: Push an interface past conventional limits using the full power of the browser; enhances how an interface feels, never what the product does.

nodes.label: Simplicity removes obstacles, not features
nodes.rationale: Simplicity is not about removing features; it is about removing obstacles between users and their goals. Every element should justify its existence, but necessary functionality, accessibility and decision-making information must survive.

nodes.label: Server-side validation always
nodes.rationale: Never trust client-side validation alone; validate and sanitize all inputs server-side, protect against injection, rate-limit.

nodes.label: Measure before and after
nodes.rationale: Premature optimization wastes time; optimize the biggest bottleneck first, on real devices and real network conditions, never sacrificing accessibility or functionality.

nodes.label: Context determines what extraordinary means
nodes.rationale: A particle system on a portfolio is impressive and on a settings page embarrassing; a settings page with instant optimistic saves is extraordinary too. Iterate with browser automation because ambitious effects never work first try.

nodes.label: Orientation and foldables: landscape restructures, never clips; react to posture and hinge
nodes.norm_label: orientation and foldables: landscape restructures, never clips; react to posture and hinge
nodes.rationale: Lock orientation only when the task truly demands it, never to dodge a layout bug.

nodes.label: Adaptation strategies per target context (desktop→mobile, tablet hybrid, mobile→desktop, screen→print, web→email)
nodes.norm_label: adaptation strategies per target context (desktop→mobile, tablet hybrid, mobile→desktop, screen→print, web→email)

nodes.norm_label: safe areas via env(safe-area-inset-*) and viewport-fit=cover

nodes.norm_label: touch targets 44x44px minimum, more spacing, no hover-dependent interactions

nodes.norm_label: 48×48 dp minimum touch target with at least 8 dp between targets

nodes.norm_label: edge-to-edge with window insets (status bar, navigation bar, display cutout, ime)

nodes.label: Material Design 3 governs structure, navigation and interaction; brand expresses through Material theming
nodes.norm_label: material design 3 governs structure, navigation and interaction; brand expresses through material theming
nodes.rationale: On native the visitor mode narrows what expression may override; a Material-everywhere cross-platform app shipping to iPhone still owes iOS its OS guarantees (safe-area insets, Reduce Motion, edge-swipe back).

nodes.norm_label: native audit health score: accessibility (voiceover/talkback), performance, appearance & theming, platform conformance, adaptivity (/20)

nodes.label: Platform Conformance verdict (start here): native app or ported website?
nodes.norm_label: platform conformance verdict (start here): native app or ported website?
nodes.rationale: Checks broken system gestures, inset violations, off-platform navigation, web-shaped controls, icon drift and system drift, scored against the platform slop tests.

nodes.label: Responsive check: interactive elements < 44x44px, fixed widths, horizontal scroll, text scaling
nodes.norm_label: responsive check: interactive elements < 44x44px, fixed widths, horizontal scroll, text scaling

nodes.label: Adaptation is rethinking the experience for the new context, not scaling pixels
nodes.norm_label: adaptation is rethinking the experience for the new context, not scaling pixels
nodes.rationale: The trap is treating adaptation as scaling; identify source assumptions (large screen, mouse, fast connection) and what won't fit, won't work (hover on touch) or is inappropriate in the target.

nodes.label: Content-driven breakpoints (640/768/1024 usually suffice; clamp() and container queries for fluid values)
nodes.norm_label: content-driven breakpoints (640/768/1024 usually suffice; clamp() and container queries for fluid values)
nodes.rationale: Don't chase device sizes; start narrow, stretch until the design breaks, add the breakpoint there. Generic breakpoints used blindly are a NEVER.

nodes.label: Mobile-first: base styles for mobile, layer complexity with min-width queries
nodes.norm_label: mobile-first: base styles for mobile, layer complexity with min-width queries
nodes.rationale: Desktop-first (max-width) means mobile loads unnecessary styles first.

nodes.label: Phone → tablet: restructure, don't stretch; drive structure from size classes / window size classes
nodes.norm_label: phone → tablet: restructure, don't stretch; drive structure from size classes / window size classes
nodes.rationale: A scaled-up phone UI on a tablet is the failure mode. Tab bar becomes sidebar/rail, sheets become popovers, list+detail side by side. Multitasking (iPad Split View, Android multi-window) hands you a phone-width window on a tablet, so size-class-driven layout handles both for free; never use device-model checks.

nodes.label: Platform → platform: translate idioms, never transplant (iOS ↔ Android table)
nodes.norm_label: platform → platform: translate idioms, never transplant (ios ↔ android table)
nodes.rationale: Tab bar ↔ navigation bar/rail/drawer, edge-swipe back ↔ predictive Back, action sheet ↔ bottom sheet, SF Symbols/SF Pro/Dynamic Type ↔ Material Symbols/Roboto/sp. Rebuild navigation and controls in the target's vocabulary; carry the brand's expressive layer through the target's theming system.

nodes.label: Web → native: reconform, don't reflow
nodes.rationale: Replace web navigation with the platform's model, HTML-shaped controls with platform controls, hover with touch-first affordances, px type with Dynamic Type / sp; the platform reference's slop test is the acceptance bar.

nodes.label: Never hide core functionality on mobile; same information architecture across contexts
nodes.norm_label: never hide core functionality on mobile; same information architecture across contexts
nodes.rationale: If it matters, make it work; different IA per context confuses users; mobile users expect mobile patterns.

nodes.label: Detect input method with pointer/hover media queries, not screen size
nodes.norm_label: detect input method with pointer/hover media queries, not screen size
nodes.rationale: Screen size doesn't tell you input method (touchscreen laptop, tablet with keyboard); touch users can't hover so hover must never carry functionality.

nodes.label: Test on real devices; DevTools emulation is not enough
nodes.norm_label: test on real devices; devtools emulation is not enough
nodes.rationale: Emulation misses touch interactions, real CPU/memory constraints, network latency, font rendering and browser chrome/keyboard; cheap Android phones reveal performance issues simulators never show.

nodes.label: Verify via adb: screencap from emulator/device, `cmd uimode night yes`, `font_scale 1.3`
nodes.norm_label: verify via adb: screencap from emulator/device, `cmd uimode night yes`, `font_scale 1.3`
nodes.rationale: Screenshots never come from a browser; capture every shipped device class; dark theme and font scale belong in the pass because a fixed layout hides clipped labels. Emulators give breadth; gestures, refresh rates and performance need hardware, and the report says which produced the evidence.

nodes.label: The Android slop test: would a fluent Android user trust this app?
nodes.norm_label: the android slop test: would a fluent android user trust this app?
nodes.rationale: The most common tell is an iOS app wearing Android's skin: bottom-only navigation copied from iPhone, a back arrow that ignores the system Back gesture, Cupertino-shaped switches and dialogs. Material 3 is the rulebook.

nodes.label: One FAB, one primary action; snackbars for transient feedback, dialogs only for interrupting decisions
nodes.norm_label: one fab, one primary action; snackbars for transient feedback, dialogs only for interrupting decisions

nodes.label: System Back always works: honor predictive Back gesture and button
nodes.norm_label: system back always works: honor predictive back gesture and button
nodes.rationale: Never trap the user or hijack the gesture.

nodes.label: Native audit from source (SwiftUI/UIKit/Compose/RN/Flutter); no browser tooling or `impeccable detect`
nodes.norm_label: native audit from source (swiftui/uikit/compose/rn/flutter); no browser tooling or `impeccable detect`
nodes.rationale: Score against the platform reference(s) ios.md / android.md (both for adaptive); the report skeleton mirrors audit.md and the two must stay in sync.

nodes.rationale: Each persona exposes failure modes a single design-director view misses; report what broke for them, not generic descriptions. Only invent project personas when real Design Context exists.

nodes.norm_label: persona casey: distracted mobile user (thumb zone, interruptions, slow connection, 44×44pt targets)
